sources.excerpt: Queen are a British rock band formed in London in 1970 by Freddie Mercury (lead vocals, piano), Brian May (guitar, vocals), and Roger Taylor (drums, vocals), later joined by John Deacon (bass).
The Beach Boys are an American rock band formed in Hawthorne, California, in 1961.
U2 are an Irish rock band formed in Dublin in 1976.
David Robert Jones (8 January 1947 – 10 January 2016), known as David Bowie, was an English singer, songwriter and actor.
Bob Dylan (legally Robert Dylan; born Robert Allen Zimmerman, May 24, 1941) is an American singer-songwriter.
Enya is the best-selling Irish solo artist, and the second-best-selling music act from Ireland overall, after the band U2.
Abbey Road is the eleventh studio album by the English rock band the Beatles, released on 26 September 1969 by Apple Records.
Thriller is the sixth studio album by the American singer and songwriter Michael Jackson.
The Joshua Tree is the fifth studio album by the Irish rock band U2.

editorNotes: An album takes its nationality from the artist who made it, so the album row was chosen to match the column above it: Abbey Road is by the English band the Beatles, Thriller by the American singer Michael Jackson and The Joshua Tree by the Irish band U2. That is the only place a reader might hesitate, because U2 appears in the grid as a band and again, indirectly, as the makers of The Joshua Tree; the two are separate tiles and neither can take the other's row, since U2 is not an album and The Joshua Tree is not a group of musicians. The three rows do not overlap at all: Queen, The Beach Boys and U2 are groups, David Bowie, Bob Dylan and Enya sing alone, and the last three tiles are records. Within each row the nationality is fixed by the sources, so exactly one placement works. Enya rather than a Northern Irish singer was chosen for the Irish column because she was born and raised in the Republic and is described plainly as Irish.
